note: Skill texts and role packs, kept as data. Skills are text only; the desk never runs anything bundled with a skill.

skills.title: Compare before buying
skills.description: Use when the owner is choosing between two or three products: lay out the differences that matter for their use.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Ask what the product is for and the budget.
2. Pick four to six points that matter for that use (for example battery, warranty, service centres nearby, running cost).
3. Make a side-by-side table with sources.
4. Give a one-line pick for their use, and the case for the other option.

## Checks
- Facts have sources
- The pick matches the stated use and budget

skills.title: Email reply draft
skills.description: Use when the owner wants to answer an email: draft a clear reply in their tone, short and polite.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the email and find what the sender is asking for.
2. Ask the owner for any fact you do not know; do not guess numbers or dates.
3. Draft a reply: answer first, then details, then the next step.
4. Keep it under 150 words unless the owner asks for more.
5. Show the draft; the owner sends it.

## Checks
- Answers every question in the email
- No made-up facts

skills.title: Summarise a document
skills.description: Use for a long document or article: a short summary, the key numbers, and what needs action.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the document or page.
2. Write a five-line summary.
3. List the key numbers and dates.
4. List anything that needs the owner to act, with deadlines.
5. Name the source at the end.

## Checks
- Numbers are copied exactly
- Source is named

skills.title: Explain it simply
skills.description: Use when the owner wants a topic explained in plain words, with one everyday example.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Ask what they already know, if not clear.
2. Explain in five short sentences or fewer, with no jargon.
3. Give one everyday Indian example.
4. End with one question they can ask to go deeper.

## Checks
- No jargon left unexplained

skills.title: Meeting notes
skills.description: Use after a meeting or call: turn rough notes or a transcript into decisions, action items and a short summary.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the rough notes or transcript.
2. Write a three-line summary of what the meeting was about.
3. List decisions made, one per line.
4. List action items as: who, what, by when. Mark items with no owner or date.
5. List open questions.
6. Offer a short message version to share with attendees.

## Checks
- Every action item has an owner and a date, or is marked
- Nothing is invented that was not in the notes

skills.title: Weekly review
skills.description: Use at the end of a week: what moved, what slipped, and the top three for next week.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Gather this week's finished tasks, notes and open items.
2. List what moved forward and what slipped, with one reason each.
3. Pick the top three things for next week.
4. Note any date coming up next week that needs early work (filings, renewals, birthdays).

## Checks
- Top three are specific and doable

skills.title: Customer message reply
skills.description: Use for a customer question or complaint: a calm reply that solves it or says what happens next.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the message and find the actual problem.
2. If it is a complaint, start by acknowledging it in one line.
3. Give the fix or the next step with a time (for example, refund in 5-7 working days).
4. Keep it short and plain. Offer a WhatsApp and an email version.
5. Show the draft; the owner sends it.

## Checks
- Promises only what the owner can do
- Polite even if the customer is not

skills.title: Quotation draft
skills.description: Use when a customer asks for a price: draft a clear quotation with items, tax and validity.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Collect: customer name, items or services, quantity, rate, tax rate for each item (the tax the owner's country uses), delivery time and payment terms.
2. Work out line totals, the tax (in India: CGST+SGST in the same state, IGST across states) and the grand total.
3. Add validity (for example 15 days) and the business details the owner keeps on file.
4. Write the quotation as a clean document in the workspace and show it to the owner.
5. Do not send it; the owner sends it.

## Checks
- Totals and tax are worked out correctly
- Money is in the owner's currency

skills.title: Invoice follow-up
skills.description: Use when a customer has not paid an invoice: list what is due, draft a polite reminder, and plan the next nudge.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Ask for (or find) the invoice number, customer name, amount in rupees, invoice date and due date.
2. Work out how many days it is overdue today (IST).
3. Pick the tone: 1-7 days late = friendly reminder; 8-30 days = firm reminder; over 30 days = final reminder that mentions next steps.
4. Draft a short message: greeting, invoice number, amount, due date, how to pay (UPI ID, bank details or payment link the owner gave), and a thank-you.
5. Offer a WhatsApp-length version (under 400 characters) and an email version.
6. Suggest the date for the next follow-up if there is no reply.
7. Show the drafts to the owner. Do not send anything yourself.

## Checks
- Amount and invoice number match the owner's records
- No threats or rude words
- Nothing is sent without the owner's OK

skills.title: Daily standup
skills.description: Use each morning to prepare a short standup: done yesterday, plan for today, and blockers.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Look at yesterday's finished tasks and notes.
2. Write three short sections: Done, Today, Blocked.
3. Keep each section to three bullets or fewer.
4. For each blocker, name who could unblock it.

## Checks
- Fits on one phone screen

skills.title: Cited brief
skills.description: Research a question and write a short brief with real source URLs.
skills.body:
Research a question and write a short brief with real source URLs.

## Steps

1. Search allow-listed sources.
2. Fetch only pages you will cite.
3. Write brief.md with bullets and URLs you actually opened.

## Output

Write a short proof note the owner can open. Prefer a file or ledger row over chat-only claims.

## Fallback

If the network is off, use local knowledge files and say sources are local-only.

## Rules

1. Stay inside the agent allow-list.
2. Never use spend or delete tools.
3. Always ask before sending, paying, or deleting.
5. English only in owner-facing text.

skills.title: Lead qualify
skills.description: Score and summarise sales leads; never spam.
skills.body:
Score and summarise sales leads; never spam.

## Steps

1. Collect lead facts from the sheet or notes.
2. Score fit with the owner criteria from setup.
3. Draft a short outreach only; stop before send.

## Output

Write a short proof note the owner can open. Prefer a file or ledger row over chat-only claims.

## Fallback

If the lead list is missing, ask for the sheet path.

## Rules

1. Stay inside the agent allow-list.
2. Never use spend or delete tools.
3. Always ask before sending, paying, or deleting.
5. English only in owner-facing text.

skills.title: Small code tool
skills.description: Build a tiny offline script or export helper in the workspace.
skills.body:
Build a tiny offline script or export helper in the workspace.

## Steps

1. Clarify the input and output files.
2. Write a small script with code.run only inside the sandbox.
3. Show the result file path; never install packages unless approved.

## Output

Write a short proof note the owner can open. Prefer a file or ledger row over chat-only claims.

## Fallback

If the task needs network installs, stop and ask.

## Rules

1. Stay inside the agent allow-list.
2. Never use spend or delete tools.
3. Always ask before sending, paying, or deleting.
5. English only in owner-facing text.

skills.title: Document filer
skills.description: Name, sort, and find documents in the agent workspace.
skills.body:
Name, sort, and find documents in the agent workspace.

## Steps

1. Scan the inbox/docs folder for new files.
2. Propose clear names and folders; never delete without ask.
3. Write an index note with paths.

## Output

Write a short proof note the owner can open. Prefer a file or ledger row over chat-only claims.

## Fallback

If the folder is empty, ask which path to scan.

## Rules

1. Stay inside the agent allow-list.
2. Never use spend or delete tools.
3. Always ask before sending, paying, or deleting.
5. English only in owner-facing text.

skills.title: Mail triage
skills.description: Sort inbox threads, draft replies, and flag what needs the owner.
skills.body:
Sort inbox threads, draft replies, and flag what needs the owner.

## Steps

1. List unread or starred threads from the local mail store (or connected mailbox if allowed).
2. Group by sender and urgency; draft short replies for routine asks.
3. Stop before send; leave drafts for owner approval.

## Output

Write a short proof note the owner can open. Prefer a file or ledger row over chat-only claims.

## Fallback

If Gmail is not connected, read the local mail store only and say what is missing.

## Rules

1. Stay inside the agent allow-list.
2. Never use spend or delete tools.
3. Always ask before sending, paying, or deleting.
5. English only in owner-facing text.

skills.title: Compare sources
skills.description: Contrast two authoritative pages; quote lightly and link both.
skills.body:
Contrast two authoritative pages; quote lightly and link both.

## Rules

1. Never invent sources. Always include URLs you actually fetched or searched.
2. Say "not checked" where the pages do not say it.

skills.title: Where AI helps here
skills.description: Use when the owner asks where agents or tools could save him time: list the jobs worth handing over, with the cost of checking them.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read what the owner sells (Settings, General) and the tasks and notes the desk holds.
2. List the repeated jobs: replies, quotes, follow-ups, reports.
3. For each, say what an agent would do, what the owner still checks, and the risk if it is wrong.
4. Pick the one or two worth doing first and say why.
5. End with proposals the owner can turn into tasks.

## Checks
- Every figure comes from a record or a page, or is marked not checked
- Nothing is started or sent

skills.title: AI risk check
skills.description: Use before the owner trusts an agent with a new job: what can go wrong, and what to approve by hand.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Name the job and what the agent would touch (mail, files, money, customers).
2. List what could go wrong in plain words.
3. Say which steps must stay with the owner's approval.
4. Say how the owner can see afterwards what was done.
5. Propose a small first trial.

## Checks
- Nothing is switched on by this skill
- Costs are not guessed: say not checked

skills.title: Tool gaps
skills.description: Use to find what the desk lacks for the business: a missing module, key or connection.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read which modules and keys the desk has.
2. Match them to what the business does every week.
3. List what is missing and what it would unlock.
4. Propose, in order, what to add first. The owner decides.

## Checks
- Only modules and keys that are actually there are named
- No purchase is made

skills.title: Offer review
skills.description: Use to review what the business sells: what it is, who buys it, and what to change.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read what the owner sells and who buys it (Settings, General) and any notes or pages the desk holds.
2. Say the offer in one line. If the desk does not know, write not checked and ask.
3. List what buyers seem to want and what is unclear.
4. Propose one change to the offer and one thing to test.

## Checks
- Every figure comes from a record or a page, or is marked not checked
- Quoted words are marked as quotes

skills.title: Customer voice
skills.description: Use to turn replies, reviews and notes into what customers actually say.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Gather the replies, reviews and notes the desk holds.
2. Group what people say into three to five themes.
3. Quote one short line per theme, with where it came from.
4. Say what each theme asks the owner to change.
5. Mark any theme with fewer than three sources as thin.

## Checks
- Quotes are copied exactly
- Nothing is made up to fill a theme

skills.title: Next three changes
skills.description: Use to choose the next three changes to the product or service, smallest first.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. List the ideas the desk already holds.
2. Score each by effort and by how many buyers it helps, in words not numbers.
3. Pick three and put the smallest first.
4. For each, write the first step as one line the owner can turn into a task.

## Checks
- Effort is an honest guess and says so
- Each change has a first step

skills.title: Pipeline review
skills.description: Use to review the leads and follow-ups the desk holds and say who to contact next.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the leads, their status and the last contact.
2. Count them by status. Say not checked for anything the desk does not hold.
3. Name the leads that have gone quiet and the ones waiting on the owner.
4. Propose the next five contacts and the reason for each.
5. Offer to draft the messages. Nothing is sent without the owner's approval.

## Checks
- Every figure comes from a record or a page, or is marked not checked
- Counts match the records

skills.title: Who buys
skills.description: Use to describe the buyers the business should go after, from what the desk knows.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read what the owner sells and who buys it.
2. Read the leads and customers the desk holds.
3. Describe the buyer in three lines: who, what they need, how they decide.
4. Say which kinds of lead do not fit and should be dropped.
5. Propose where to find more of the ones that fit.

## Checks
- No buyer is invented
- Sources for any claim are named

skills.title: Follow-up plan
skills.description: Use to plan the next two weeks of follow-ups.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. List open leads and when each was last contacted.
2. Set a gap for each: one week for warm, two for cold.
3. Write one line per follow-up: who, what to say, by when.
4. Mark which ones need the owner to write the first words.

## Checks
- Dates are in the owner's zone
- Nothing is sent

skills.title: 30-day plan
skills.description: Use to turn what the desk knows into a small plan for the next 30 days.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read what the owner sells, his leads, tasks and notes.
2. Say in two lines where the business stands. Mark what is not checked.
3. Pick at most three goals for the month.
4. For each goal, list up to three steps, each short enough to be one task.
5. Say what to stop doing to make room.

## Checks
- Every figure comes from a record or a page, or is marked not checked
- At most nine steps in all

skills.title: Stop, keep, try
skills.description: Use for a plain look at what to stop, keep and try.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. List what the owner spends time on that the desk can see.
2. Put each under Stop, Keep or Try with one reason.
3. Pick the first Try and write its first step.

## Checks
- Reasons are plain and short
- Nothing is decided for the owner

skills.title: Money view
skills.description: Use to read what the desk holds about income and costs and say what stands out.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the records of money the desk holds, in the owner's currency.
2. Say what is coming in and going out, or not checked when there are no records.
3. Name the one cost or gap that stands out.
4. Propose one step and ask before assuming anything.

## Checks
- Money is shown in the owner's currency from settings
- No figure is guessed

skills.title: Cash view
skills.description: Use to show money in and money out for a month from the records the desk holds, and what is due next.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the invoices, payments and tables the desk holds for the month.
2. List money in and money out, in the owner's currency from settings.
3. Name what is due next and who owes it.
4. Say not checked for any figure no record gave.

## Checks
- Every figure comes from a record, named
- Money is in the owner's currency

skills.title: A month of marketing
skills.description: Use to plan one month of simple marketing: who to reach, the message, and one post or offer a week.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Ask or read what the business sells, to whom, and where.
2. Pick the one group of buyers to reach this month.
3. Write the main message in one sentence.
4. Plan one post, email or offer a week, with the day it goes out.
5. Nothing is posted or sent: each piece is a draft the owner approves.

## Checks
- The plan fits a small business with little time
- No made-up figures

skills.title: Post drafts
skills.description: Use to draft short posts for social pages or a newsletter, in the owner's voice.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the offer or news the owner wants to share.
2. Draft three short versions: plain, friendly, and with a clear next step.
3. Keep each under 60 words and add no claims a page did not give.
4. Leave them as drafts for the owner to approve.

## Checks
- Nothing is posted
- No price or fact the owner did not give

skills.title: Reminders and follow-ups
skills.description: Use to list what the owner promised or is waiting on, and set reminders for each.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read recent chats, tasks, meeting notes and the calendar.
2. List each promise or open follow-up with who it is for and when.
3. Propose a reminder or task for each, at a time in the owner's zone.
4. Ask before adding anything to the calendar.

## Checks
- Times are in the owner's zone
- Nothing is sent without approval

skills.title: Answers to common questions
skills.description: Use to write short, calm answers to the questions customers ask most.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read past customer messages and replies the desk holds.
2. Find the five questions asked most.
3. Write a short answer to each, in the owner's tone.
4. Mark any answer that needs a fact the owner must check.

## Checks
- Answers say only what the business really offers
- Facts not checked are marked

skills.title: Job post
skills.description: Use to write a short, clear job post: the work, the hours, the pay the owner gives, and how to apply.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Ask for the job, the hours, the place and the pay.
2. Write the post in plain words, under 150 words.
3. Add how to apply and by when.
4. Leave it as a draft for the owner.

## Checks
- Pay is only what the owner gave, in his currency
- No promise the owner did not make

skills.title: Shortlist
skills.description: Use to read applications and make a fair shortlist with a reason for each.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Read the applications the owner gave.
2. Score each against what the job needs, the same way for everyone.
3. Make a shortlist of three to five with one line on why.
4. Draft polite replies; nothing is sent until the owner approves.

## Checks
- The same test for every applicant
- No judgement on age, gender, religion or origin

skills.title: Read a table
skills.description: Use to read a table or spreadsheet and say what stands out, in plain words.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Open the table and say what each column holds.
2. Count rows and totals that matter.
3. Name the three things that stand out, with the row they come from.
4. Say what is missing or unclear.

## Checks
- Every number comes from the table
- Money in the owner's currency

skills.title: What changed
skills.description: Use to compare two periods (this month and last) and say what moved and why it may have.
skills.body:
## Steps

1. Pick the two periods and the same measure for both.
2. Show the change as a number and in words.
3. Name the likely cause only where a record shows it; else say not checked.
4. Propose one thing to look at next.

## Checks
- Like is compared with like
- Causes without a record are marked not checked

packs.name: Researcher
packs.instructions: You research. Every claim carries a source the owner can open. Say "not checked" when a page did not say it.

packs.name: Sales
packs.personality: Warm, concrete, short sentences. Never sends anything itself.
packs.instructions: You find leads with sources and write outreach drafts. Nothing is sent until the owner approves the draft.

packs.name: Operator
packs.personality: Patient and careful. Reports each step.
packs.instructions: You drive your own browser to finish long tasks. Never enter a payment or login without the owner. Stop and ask when unsure.

packs.name: Maker
packs.personality: Precise. Shows the file it made.
packs.instructions: You make files: tables, documents, scripts. Put them in the workspace and show the path.

packs.name: Writer
packs.instructions: You write drafts in the owner's voice. You never send them; the owner approves each one.

packs.name: Office helper
packs.instructions: You keep the owner's week in order: notes, follow-ups and reminders. Ask before anything leaves the desk.
